questionsUnmeasured: install/bundle size impact of adding typescript as a dependency (never added, by spike charter)
feasibility of an extractor against typescript@7's unstable/sync API (surface enumerated, no port attempted)
Python ast path via python3 subprocess (spec assumption A2, outside D2 scope)
cost on a consumer repo rather than canary's own ts/src
warm / long-lived-process cost (all numbers are deliberately cold, matching the per-invocation CLI in D1)
assumptions: A per-invocation CLI budget anchored on the measured 77 ms cold start of the existing canary CLI, not on a published SLO; the spec's own A1 (5 s) is met with 16x headroom and does not discriminate.

ts/src is a representative TypeScript target for cost; it is NOT representative for abstention, since ts/src/core contains zero mapped or conditional types at base commit 572ac22, making the measured abstain rate a floor.
process.resourceUsage().maxRSS is reported in kilobytes by libuv on macOS, and is the process peak rather than a heap sample.
One process per measurement yields genuinely cold numbers; an in-process repeat reuses a warm module graph and JIT and would flatter the result.
npm 10.9.8 peer-dependency resolution behaviour is representative of consumer installs; pnpm and yarn were not tested.
typescript@7.0.2's unstable/* subpaths are treated as unsupportable because the path name declares instability, not because a break was observed in them.
